claim: The bithorax complex (BX-C) in Drosophila melanogaster is a cluster of homeotic genes that determine body segment identity.
source: The bithorax complex (BX-C) in Drosophila melanogaster is a cluster of homeotic genes that determine body segment identity.
evidence: This is a direct statement from the abstract describing the function of the BX-C.

claim: Expression of BX-C genes is governed by cis-regulatory domains, one for each parasegment.
source: Expression of these genes is governed by cis-regulatory domains, one for each parasegment.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a known feature of BX-C organization.

claim: Stable repression of BX-C regulatory domains depends on Polycomb Group (PcG) functions.
source: Stable repression of these domains depends on Polycomb Group (PcG) functions, which include trimethylation of lysine 27 of histone H3 (H3K27me3).
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and is supported by established knowledge about PcG function.

claim: Polycomb Group functions include trimethylation of lysine 27 of histone H3 (H3K27me3).
source: Stable repression of these domains depends on Polycomb Group (PcG) functions, which include trimethylation of lysine 27 of histone H3 (H3K27me3).
evidence: This is a direct statement about PcG molecular function.

claim: H3K27me3 profiles across the BX-C in successive parasegments showed a 'stairstep' pattern.
source: The H3K27me3 profiles across the BX-C in successive parasegments showed a 'stairstep' pattern that revealed sharp boundaries of the BX-C regulatory domains.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and shown in Figure 2C-F.

claim: The stairstep pattern of H3K27me3 revealed sharp boundaries of the BX-C regulatory domains.
source: The H3K27me3 profiles across the BX-C in successive parasegments showed a 'stairstep' pattern that revealed sharp boundaries of the BX-C regulatory domains.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and demonstrated in Figure 2.

claim: Acetylated H3K27 was broadly enriched across active domains in a pattern complementary to H3K27me3.
source: Acetylated H3K27 was broadly enriched across active domains, in a pattern complementary to H3K27me3.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and shown in Figure 3B,C.

claim: CTCF bound the borders between H3K27 modification domains.
source: The CCCTC-binding protein (CTCF) bound the borders between H3K27 modification domains; it was retained even in parasegments where adjacent domains lack H3K27me3.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and shown in Figure 2G-H.

claim: CTCF was retained at domain borders even in parasegments where adjacent domains lack H3K27me3.
source: The CCCTC-binding protein (CTCF) bound the borders between H3K27 modification domains; it was retained even in parasegments where adjacent domains lack H3K27me3.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and demonstrated in Figure 2H.

claim: A mutation in Polycomb was discovered for its segmental transformations.
source: Indeed, a mutation in Polycomb, the founding member of the PcG, was discovered for its segmental transformations (Lewis, 1947).
evidence: This is a historical fact cited from Lewis, 1947.

claim: The BX-C contains three homeobox-containing genes: Ultrabithorax (Ubx), abdominal-A (abd-A), and Abdominal-B (Abd-B).
source: The regulatory domains control three homeobox-containing genes of the complex, Ultrabithorax (Ubx), abdominal-A (abd-A), and Abdominal-B (Abd-B) (Maeda and Karch, 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citation to Maeda and Karch, 2009.

claim: The BX-C regulatory domains encompass nine regulatory domains, each for a different parasegment.
source: The genetic functions are now thought to encompass nine regulatory domains, each for a different parasegment.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as current understanding.

claim: The entire BX-C is heavily marked with H3K27me3 in whole embryos.
source: The entire BX-C is heavily marked with H3K27me3 in whole embryos (Schuettengruber et al., 2009; Nègre et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated with citations to prior studies.

claim: H3K27me3 is necessary for maintaining repression of BX-C genes.
source: This histone modification is necessary for maintaining repression of BX-C genes (Pengelly et al., 2013), yet these genes are not repressed throughout the body.
evidence: This is stated with citation to Pengelly et al., 2013.

claim: Papp and Müller (2006) observed loss of the K27me3 mark across the Ubx transcription unit in haltere and third leg imaginal discs.
source: Indeed, Papp and Müller (2006) observed loss of the K27me3 mark across the Ubx transcription unit in haltere and third leg imaginal discs, tissues where Ubx is transcribed.
evidence: This is a citation of prior work by Papp and Müller.

claim: Single parasegments were marked with a combination of Gal4 and Gal80 drivers.
source: To address this, we marked single parasegments with a combination of Gal4 and Gal80 drivers, and developed a nuclear sorting-chromatin immunoprecipitation-sequencing protocol.
evidence: This describes the experimental approach used in the study.

claim: Gal80 binds to and inactivates Gal4, leaving Gal4 activity in a single parasegment.
source: Gal80 binds to and inactivates Gal4, leaving Gal4 activity in a single parasegment (Figure 1A).
evidence: This describes the mechanism of the Gal4/Gal80 system used in the study.

claim: The largest differences in H3K27me3 enrichment between parasegments occurred at the BX-C.
source: The largest differences in H3K27me3 enrichment between parasegments occurred at the BX-C (Figure 2A, Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results and shown in Figure 2A and supplement.

claim: The BX-C exhibited a striking 'stairstep' pattern of H3K27me3 enrichment across parasegments PS4-PS7.
source: While the H3K27me3 profiles in our four adjacent parasegments were very similar elsewhere in the genome (Figure 2—figure supplement 1), the BX-C exhibited a striking 'stairstep' pattern.
evidence: This is a primary finding shown in Figure 2C-F.

claim: Large expanses of H3K27me3 enrichment were lost as we moved from anterior to posterior along the body axis.
source: Large expanses of H3K27me3 enrichment were lost as we moved from anterior to posterior along the body axis (Figure 2C–F), revealing the locations of the regulatory domains.
evidence: This is a primary finding shown in Figure 2C-F.

claim: The BX-C is almost completely repressed in PS4, with only a few neuronal cells on the midline showing UBX expression in embryos.
source: The BX-C is almost completely repressed in PS4, with only a few neuronal cells on the midline showing UBX expression in embryos.
evidence: This is stated in the results section describing PS4 H3K27me3 patterns.

claim: The PS5 regulatory domain is defined by the low level of H3K27me3 modification across the leftmost (proximal) 92 kb of the complex.
source: The PS5 regulatory domain, associated with the bithorax (bx) mutant lesions, is defined by the low level of H3K27me3 modification across the leftmost (proximal) 92 kb of the complex (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results and shown in Figure 2D.

claim: There is a sharp transition to full H3K27me3 coverage at a position upstream of the Ubx transcription start site in PS5.
source: There is a sharp transition to full H3K27me3 coverage at a position upstream of the Ubx transcription start site.
evidence: This is stated in the results describing PS5 and shown in Figure 2D.

claim: In PS6, the leftmost 137 kb of the BX-C is clear of the K27me3 mark.
source: In PS6, the leftmost 137 kb of the BX-C is clear of the K27me3 mark (Figure 2E); the additional K27me3-clear region reveals the PS6 domain.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results and shown in Figure 2E.

claim: The transition point to full K27 methylation in PS6 coincides with the genetically defined Fub border between the PS6 and the PS7 regulatory domains.
source: The transition point to full K27 methylation coincides with the genetically defined Fub border between the PS6 and the PS7 regulatory domains (Bender and Lucas, 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the results with citation to Bender and Lucas, 2013.

claim: In PS7, an additional 36 kb was depleted of H3K27me3.
source: In PS7, an additional 36 kb was depleted of H3K27me3 (Figure 2F).
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results and shown in Figure 2F.

claim: The PS7 H3K27me3-depleted region includes the abd-A transcription unit and is associated with the infraabdominal-2 (iab-2) class of genetic mutations.
source: This region includes the abd-A transcription unit, and is associated with the infraabdominal-2 (iab-2) class of genetic mutations.
evidence: This is stated in the results describing PS7.

claim: A reproducible mound of H3K27me3 was observed in PS7 nuclei close to the Ubx promoter.
source: We observed a reproducible mound of H3K27me3 in PS7 nuclei close to the Ubx promoter (arrow in Figure 2F).
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results and shown in Figure 2F.

claim: The H3K27me3 mound near the Ubx promoter in PS7 may reflect repression of Ubx by abd-A in this parasegment, mediated by the PcG.
source: This may reflect repression of Ubx by abd-A in this parasegment (Karch et al., 1990), mediated by the PcG.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation with citation to Karch et al., 1990.

claim: The sharp discontinuities in K27 methylation coincide with binding sites of CTCF.
source: The sharp discontinuities in K27 methylation coincide with binding sites of the CCCTC-binding factor (CTCF), which is thought to impose boundaries on regulatory domains in many systems (Ohlsson et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 2G-H, with citation to Ohlsson et al., 2010.

claim: CTCF in PS7 nuclei gives a pattern virtually identical to the whole embryo pattern.
source: CTCF in PS7 nuclei gives a pattern virtually identical to the whole embryo pattern (Figure 2H).
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results and shown in Figure 2H.

claim: The activation state of a domain is not coupled to the presence of CTCF at its borders.
source: Apparently, the activation state of a domain is not coupled to the presence of CTCF at its borders.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the observation that CTCF patterns are similar in active and repressed states.

claim: CTCF is present in a protein complex with Centrosomal Protein 190 (CP190).
source: CTCF is present in a protein complex with Centrosomal Protein 190 (CP190) (Mohan et al., 2007), and the binding sites of these proteins often overlap (Nègre et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated with citations to Mohan et al., 2007 and Nègre et al., 2010.

claim: The binding sites of CTCF and CP190 often overlap.
source: CTCF is present in a protein complex with Centrosomal Protein 190 (CP190) (Mohan et al., 2007), and the binding sites of these proteins often overlap (Nègre et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated with citation to Nègre et al., 2010.

claim: CP190 sites largely coincide with CTCF sites in the BX-C.
source: The CP190 sites largely coincide with CTCF sites in the BX-C, and, as with CTCF, there is little difference between the CP190 pattern in unsorted nuclei (Figure 2I; Nègre et al., 2010) and in PS7 nuclei (Figure 2J).
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results and shown in Figure 2I-J.

claim: There is little difference between the CP190 pattern in unsorted nuclei and in PS7 nuclei.
source: The CP190 sites largely coincide with CTCF sites in the BX-C, and, as with CTCF, there is little difference between the CP190 pattern in unsorted nuclei (Figure 2I; Nègre et al., 2010) and in PS7 nuclei (Figure 2J).
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results and shown in Figure 2I-J.

claim: There is a noteworthy CP190 site immediately proximal to the 3′ end of the Ubx transcription unit, separating Ubx from the adjacent gene (modular serine protease).
source: There is a noteworthy CP190 site immediately proximal to the 3′ end of the Ubx transcription unit, separating Ubx from the adjacent gene (modular serine protease).
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results and shown in Figure 2I-J.

claim: Acetylation of H3K27 (H3K27ac) is correlated with active enhancer regions.
source: Acetylation of H3K27 (H3K27ac) is correlated with active enhancer regions (Heintzman et al., 2009; Kharchenko et al., 2011), and is anti-correlated with PcG function (Tie et al., 2009), prompting us to examine its pattern in the BX-C.
evidence: This is stated with citations to prior studies.

claim: H3K27ac is anti-correlated with PcG function.
source: Acetylation of H3K27 (H3K27ac) is correlated with active enhancer regions (Heintzman et al., 2009; Kharchenko et al., 2011), and is anti-correlated with PcG function (Tie et al., 2009), prompting us to examine its pattern in the BX-C.
evidence: This is stated with citation to Tie et al., 2009.

claim: H3K27ac showed the opposite pattern to H3K27me3 in the BX-C.
source: H3K27ac showed the opposite pattern to H3K27me3.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results and shown in Figure 3B-C.

claim: There is relatively little H3K27ac across the BX-C in unsorted nuclei.
source: There is relatively little H3K27ac across the BX-C in unsorted nuclei, but in PS7, the active domains show broad enrichment for H3K27ac (Figure 3B,C).
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results and shown in Figure 3B.

claim: In PS7, the active domains show broad enrichment for H3K27ac.
source: There is relatively little H3K27ac across the BX-C in unsorted nuclei, but in PS7, the active domains show broad enrichment for H3K27ac (Figure 3B,C).
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results and shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Within each active domain, H3K27ac coverage is boundary-to-boundary.
source: Within each domain, however, the coverage is boundary-to-boundary, although many enhancers in the BX-C are not active in embryos.
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 3C.

claim: H3K27ac is a mirror to H3K27me3, in extent, if not in density.
source: Overall, H3K27ac is a mirror to H3K27me3, in extent, if not in density.
evidence: This is a summary statement in the results based on the data in Figure 3.

claim: ChIP of serine-5-phosphorylated RNA polymerase II (Pol-II) in whole embryos shows the transcription units for Ubx, abd-A, and Abd-B.
source: ChIP of serine-5-phosphorylated RNA polymerase II (Pol-II) (transcriptionally engaged polymerase) in whole embryos shows the transcription units for Ubx, abd-A, and Abd-B (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results and shown in Figure 3D.

claim: There is an unexpected Pol-II peak ∼14.5 kb upstream of the Ubx promoter, coincident with the CTCF binding site at the border between the PS5 and PS6 domains.
source: There is an unexpected Pol-II peak ∼14.5 kb upstream of the Ubx promoter, coincident with the CTCF binding site at the border between the PS5 and PS6 domains (arrow in Figure 3D).
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results and shown in Figure 3D.

claim: Pol-II in PS7 marks the Ubx and abd-A transcription units.
source: Pol-II in PS7 (Figure 3E) marks the Ubx and abd-A transcription units, as expected from the UBX and ABD-A protein patterns (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results and shown in Figure 3E.

claim: There is a Pol-II peak at the major Abd-B promoter in PS7, although Abd-B RNA and protein are absent from PS7.
source: There is also a Pol-II peak at the major Abd-B promoter (arrow in Figure 3E), although Abd-B RNA and protein are absent from PS7 (Celniker et al., 1990; Boulet et al., 1991) and this region is H3K27 trimethylated.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results and shown in Figure 3E, with citations to Celniker et al., 1990 and Boulet et al., 1991.

claim: Analogous localization of Pol-II at the Abd-B promoter in wing and haltere discs was reported by Chopra et al. (2009), who argued that these polymerase molecules were 'paused'.
source: Analogous localization of Pol-II at the Abd-B promoter in wing and haltere discs was reported by Chopra et al. (2009), who argued that these polymerase molecules were 'paused'.
evidence: This is a citation of prior work by Chopra et al., 2009.

claim: The H3K4me3 mark aligns with the Ubx and abd-A promoters in PS7 nuclei (but not Abd-B).
source: The H3K4me3 mark aligns with the Ubx and abd-A promoters in PS7 nuclei (but not Abd-B; Figure 3G) and is reduced in mixed cells (Figure 3F); this histone mark has been seen at active promoters in other systems (Ruthenburg et al., 2007).
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results and shown in Figure 3G, with citation to Ruthenburg et al., 2007.

claim: The POLYCOMB subunit of PRC1 is known to bind to the H3K27me3 modification through its chromodomain.
source: The POLYCOMB subunit of PRC1 is known to bind to the H3K27me3 modification through its chromodomain (Fischle et al., 2003), and so PRC1 localization might be expected to correspond to the stair-step H3K27me3 pattern.
evidence: This is stated with citation to Fischle et al., 2003.

claim: PC profiles show sharp peaks at PREs in nuclei from whole embryos.
source: Our PC profiles show sharp peaks at PREs in nuclei from whole embryos (Figure 3H), matching the profile for POLYHOMEOTIC, another PRC1 subunit (Figure 3J).
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results and shown in Figure 3H.

claim: In PS7 nuclei, both POLYCOMB and POLYHOMEOTIC subunits of PRC1 are bound to the Polycomb Response Elements of the active PS6 and PS7 domains at levels comparable to those in the whole embryo profile.
source: In PS7 nuclei, we find both the POLYCOMB and POLYHOMEOTIC subunits of PRC1 are bound to the Polycomb Response Elements of the active PS6 and PS7 domains at levels comparable to those in the whole embryo profile (Figure 3H–K).
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results and shown in Figure 3H-K.

claim: In the active PS5 domain, the levels of PC and PHO at the PS5 PRE are reduced, relative to the whole embryo profile.
source: In the active PS5 domain, the levels of PC and PHO at the PS5 PRE are reduced, relative to the whole embryo profile.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results and shown in Figure 3H-K.

claim: Papp and Müller (2006) have reported reduced retention of PRC1 and 2 components at the PRE in the PS5 domain in haltere and third leg imaginal discs, where the PS5 domain is in the active state and K27me3 is absent.
source: Papp and Müller (2006) have reported reduced retention of PRC1 and 2 components at the PRE in the PS5 domain in haltere and third leg imaginal discs, where the PS5 domain is in the active state and K27me3 is absent.
evidence: This is a citation of prior work by Papp and Müller, 2006.

claim: PRC1 presence is apparently not a determinant of repressed domains, although its subunits are clearly needed for PcG repression.
source: PRC1 presence is apparently not a determinant of repressed domains, although its subunits are clearly needed for PcG repression (Simon and Kingston, 2013).
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the data, with citation to Simon and Kingston, 2013.

claim: The profiles for SU(Z)12, a PRC2 component, look similar to those of the PRC1 proteins, POLYCOMB and POLYHOMEOTIC.
source: The profiles for SU(Z)12, a PRC2 component (Figure 3L,M), look similar to those of the PRC1 proteins, POLYCOMB and POLYHOMEOTIC.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results and shown in Figure 3L-M.

claim: There are major peaks of SU(Z)12 at the known PREs in both whole embryo and PS7 nuclei.
source: There are major peaks at the known PREs in both whole embryo and PS7 nuclei, although in PS7, the PREs in active domains have reduced levels of SU(Z)12.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results and shown in Figure 3L-M.

claim: In PS7, the PREs in active domains have reduced levels of SU(Z)12.
source: There are major peaks at the known PREs in both whole embryo and PS7 nuclei, although in PS7, the PREs in active domains have reduced levels of SU(Z)12.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results and shown in Figure 3M.

claim: SU(Z)12 is present at the transcription start sites of Ubx, abd-A, and Abd-B.
source: SU(Z)12 is also present at the transcription start sites of Ubx, abd-A, and Abd-B; binding at these promoters is more apparent than it is for PRC1 proteins.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results and shown in Figure 3L-M.

claim: Binding of SU(Z)12 at the Ubx, abd-A, and Abd-B promoters is more apparent than it is for PRC1 proteins.
source: SU(Z)12 is also present at the transcription start sites of Ubx, abd-A, and Abd-B; binding at these promoters is more apparent than it is for PRC1 proteins.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results and shown in Figure 3L-M.

claim: In the PS6 domain of the BX-C, there are many enhancers to drive Ubx expression in specific cells at specific developmental times, all of which are blocked in parasegments one through five, but active in parasegments 6 through 12.
source: In the PS6 domain of the BX-C, for example, there are many enhancers to drive Ubx expression in specific cells at specific developmental times, all of which are blocked in parasegments one through five, but active in parasegments 6 through 12 (Bender and Lucas, 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with citation to Bender and Lucas, 2013.

claim: Individual enhancers in the BX-C need not include a segmental address specified by gap and pair-rule DNA-binding factors; their function is segmentally restricted by the domain architecture.
source: Individual enhancers need not include a segmental address that is specified, for example, by gap and pair-rule DNA-binding factors; their function is segmentally restricted by the domain architecture.
evidence: This is an interpretation stated in the discussion.

claim: BX-C enhancers will drive expression in a different parasegment when inserted into a different domain (as in the Cbx transposition).
source: Indeed, these enhancers will drive expression in a different parasegment when inserted into a different domain (as in the Cbx transposition, Peifer et al., 1987).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with citation to Peifer et al., 1987.

claim: Each BX-C domain has a distinctive collection of enhancers; the UBX pattern in PS5 is quite different from that in PS6.
source: Each domain has a distinctive collection of enhancers; the UBX pattern in PS5 is quite different from that in PS6.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion based on known biology.

claim: The all-or-nothing H3K27me3 coverage of the BX-C parasegmental domains validates and refines the domain model.
source: The all-or-nothing H3K27me3 coverage of the BX-C parasegmental domains validates and refines the domain model.
evidence: This is a summary statement in the discussion based on the findings.

claim: K27me3 is uniformly removed across the PS5 and PS7 domains in PS5 and PS7, even though the activated genes in those parasegments are only transcribed in a subset of cells.
source: In particular, K27me3 is uniformly removed across the PS5 and PS7 domains in PS5 and PS7, even though the activated genes in those parasegments (Ubx and abd-A, respectively) are only transcribed in a subset of cells.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion based on the findings.

claim: Both PRC1 and PRC2 components have binding patterns that do not fully reflect function (repression and K27 methylation, respectively).
source: It is interesting that both PRC1 and PRC2 components have binding patterns that do not fully reflect function (repression and K27 methylation, respectively), indicating the possibility that function of these complexes is regulated separately from binding (Papp and Müller, 2006).
evidence: This is an interpretation stated in the discussion with citation to Papp and Müller, 2006.

claim: The function of PRC1 and PRC2 complexes may be regulated separately from binding.
source: It is interesting that both PRC1 and PRC2 components have binding patterns that do not fully reflect function (repression and K27 methylation, respectively), indicating the possibility that function of these complexes is regulated separately from binding (Papp and Müller, 2006).
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation stated in the discussion.

claim: PRC2 complexes methylate histone H3 on lysine 27.
source: These include the PRC1 family of complexes, which compact chromatin and ubiquitylate histone H2A, and the PRC2 complexes, which methylate histone H3 on lysine 27.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as established knowledge.

claim: The PRC1 family of complexes compact chromatin and ubiquitylate histone H2A.
source: These include the PRC1 family of complexes, which compact chromatin and ubiquitylate histone H2A, and the PRC2 complexes, which methylate histone H3 on lysine 27.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as established knowledge.

claim: Both PRC1 and PRC2 are required to maintain repression of homeotic genes in appropriate parasegments.
source: Both PRC1 and PRC2 are required to maintain repression of homeotic genes in appropriate parasegments, so these complexes may generate segment-specific chromatin features in the regulatory domains of the BX-C.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as established knowledge.

claim: Lewis showed that mutations that transform specific segments align on the genetic map in the order of the body segments that they affect.
source: Lewis showed that mutations that transform specific segments align on the genetic map in the order of the body segments that they affect (Lewis, 1978).
evidence: This is a historical fact cited from Lewis, 1978.

claim: The evolutionary conservation of homeotic gene order, including that in the mammalian HOX complexes, suggests that chromosomal position dictates the expression pattern.
source: The evolutionary conservation of this gene order, including that in the mammalian HOX complexes, suggests that chromosomal position dictates the expression pattern.
evidence: This is an inference stated in the introduction based on evolutionary conservation.

claim: Lewis used nested deletions to show that successively more distal genetic functions of the BX-C are activated in successively more posterior segments along the body axis.
source: Lewis used nested deletions to show that successively more distal genetic functions of the BX-C are activated in successively more posterior segments along the body axis (Lewis, 1981).
evidence: This is a historical fact cited from Lewis, 1981.

claim: Enhancer traps in the BX-C show different anterior limits of expression.
source: The regulatory domains have been roughly defined by mutant lesions (Lewis, 1978), and by enhancer traps in the BX-C, which show different anterior limits of expression (Bender and Hudson, 2000).
evidence: This is stated with citation to Bender and Hudson, 2000.

claim: The molecular features that define BX-C regulatory regions, as well as the precise locations of their boundaries, have not been defined prior to this study.
source: The molecular features that define these regions, as well as the precise locations of their boundaries, have not been defined.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction to establish the gap in knowledge.

claim: Parasegment-specific patterns of histone modification might be obscured when all the parasegments are pooled for analysis.
source: It seemed likely that parasegment-specific patterns of histone modification might be obscured when all the parasegments are pooled for analysis.
evidence: This is a hypothesis stated in the introduction.

claim: The border between the PS5 and PS6 domains, defined by the discontinuity in K27me3 enrichment in PS5 nuclei, lies 14 kb upstream of the Ubx promoter.
source: In the current study, the border between the PS5 and PS6 domains, defined by the discontinuity in K27me3 enrichment in PS5 nuclei, lies 14 kb upstream of the Ubx promoter.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results.

claim: Transgenic reporter elements inserted between the Ubx promoter and the K27me3-defined border show patterns with a PS6 anterior limit.
source: However, transgenic reporter elements inserted between the Ubx promoter and the K27me3-defined border (presumably part of the PS5 regulatory domain) show patterns with a PS6 anterior limit.
evidence: This is stated in the results as a discrepancy with genetic data.

claim: An enhancer trap 3 kb downstream of the Ubx start site shows a PS4 anterior border.
source: An enhancer trap 3 kb downstream of the Ubx start site shows a PS4 anterior border (Casares et al., 1997), and a ncRNA with a PS4 anterior expression limit is transcribed from the region 5–15 kb downstream of the Ubx start (Pease et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated with citation to Casares et al., 1997.

claim: A ncRNA with a PS4 anterior expression limit is transcribed from the region 5–15 kb downstream of the Ubx start.
source: An enhancer trap 3 kb downstream of the Ubx start site shows a PS4 anterior border (Casares et al., 1997), and a ncRNA with a PS4 anterior expression limit is transcribed from the region 5–15 kb downstream of the Ubx start (Pease et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated with citation to Pease et al., 2013.

claim: Despite the activity of regulatory regions in PS4 cells, we did not detect a decrease in K27me3 at these locations.
source: Despite the activity of these regulatory regions in PS4 cells, we did not detect a decrease in K27me3 at these locations.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results.

claim: The PS4 active state may be early and transient, limited to a subset of PS4 cells, or resistant to H3K27 methylation.
source: The PS4 active state may be early and transient, limited to a subset of PS4 cells, or resistant to H3K27 methylation.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation stated in the results.

claim: CTCF is thought to impose boundaries on regulatory domains in many systems.
source: The sharp discontinuities in K27 methylation coincide with binding sites of the CCCTC-binding factor (CTCF), which is thought to impose boundaries on regulatory domains in many systems (Ohlsson et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated with citation to Ohlsson et al., 2010.

claim: The experimental conditions used do not detect robust CTCF enrichment in some BX-C locations that have been reported by others.
source: We note that our experimental conditions do not detect robust CTCF enrichment in some BX-C locations that have been reported by others (Nègre et al., 2010), notably at the border between regulatory regions for PS7 and PS8, and proximal to the 3′ end of the Ubx transcription unit.
evidence: This is stated in the results with citation to Nègre et al., 2010.

claim: In the Antennapedia complex, CP190 peaks often appear without coincident CTCF peaks.
source: In the Antennapedia complex, the other homeotic gene complex in flies, CP190 peaks often appear without coincident CTCF peaks (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results and shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: The low residual level of H3K27me3 marks in the 92 kb PS5 domain is likely due to partial contamination from more anterior parasegments in the preparation of PS5 nuclei.
source: The low residual level of H3K27me3 marks in the 92 kb PS5 domain is likely due to partial contamination from more anterior parasegments in our preparation of PS5 nuclei (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is an interpretation stated in the results.

claim: The PS6 regulatory domain is the one best defined by genetic analysis, with a series of rearrangement breakpoints giving bithoraxoid (bxd) phenotypes.
source: The PS6 regulatory domain is the one best defined by genetic analysis, with a series of rearrangement breakpoints giving bithoraxoid (bxd) phenotypes (Bender and Lucas, 2013).
evidence: This is stated with citation to Bender and Lucas, 2013.

claim: Temporal activation pattern of the Hox-D cluster in mouse correlates with loss of H3K27me3.
source: This is reminiscent of the temporal activation pattern of the Hox-D cluster in mouse, which correlates with loss of H3K27me3 (Soshnikova and Duboule, 2009).
evidence: This is stated with citation to Soshnikova and Duboule, 2009.

claim: H2A ubiquitylation promotes PRC2 recruitment and H3K27 trimethylation.
source: It will be important to map H2A ubiquitylation (a function of the dRING subunit of PRC1) across the domains, especially given recent findings that H2A ubiquitylation promotes PRC2 recruitment and H3K27 trimethylation (Blackledge et al., 2014; Cooper et al., 2014; Kalb et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated with citations to Blackledge et al., 2014; Cooper et al., 2014; Kalb et al., 2014.

claim: Kwong et al. (2008) have made analogous observations regarding PRC retention in imaginal discs of the third thoracic segment.
source: Kwong et al. (2008) have made analogous observations regarding PRC retention in imaginal discs of the third thoracic segment.
evidence: This is a citation of prior work by Kwong et al., 2008.

claim: Published ChIP–CHIP and ChIP-seq profiles for PC across the BX-C vary from broad coverage matching the H3K27me3 profile to sharp peaks at the known PREs.
source: Published ChIP–CHIP and ChIP-seq profiles for PC across the BX-C vary from broad coverage matching the H3K27me3 profile (Kwong et al., 2008) to sharp peaks at the known PREs (Gonzalez et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated with citations to Kwong et al., 2008 and Gonzalez et al., 2014.

claim: The difference in PC profiles may be due to different procedures for chromatin fragmentation prior to immunoprecipitation.
source: The difference may be due to different procedures for chromatin fragmentation prior to immunoprecipitation (Straub et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated with citation to Straub et al., 2013.

claim: Recovered nuclei constituted between 1 and 6% of total single nuclei, depending on the parasegment under selection.
source: Recovered nuclei constituted between 1 and 6% of total single nuclei (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C), depending of the parasegment under selection.
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section and shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1C.
